methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Solar panel manufacturer to establish $23.78M Shenandoah County facility
signals.signal_reading: Manufacturing investment in Shenandoah Valley suggests platform-enabled industrial automation may distribute economic activity, but without evidence of deep AI capability development, signals shallow adoption in non-metro regions.

signals.title: Two trends converge on Botetourt County: Data centers and solar farms.
signals.signal_reading: Data center infrastructure in Botetourt County creates AI compute backbone but concentrates value capture elsewhere—local opposition reflects community exclusion from capability building, reinforcing shallow engagement even as physical infrastructure arrives.

signals.title: Gigawatt data center project planned for Wythe County
signals.signal_reading: Gigawatt-scale data center in Wythe County positions Southwest Virginia as AI infrastructure provider rather than AI capability developer, extracting energy/land resources while concentrating technical expertise and economic returns in metro command centers.

signals.title: The Pulse: Virginia Tech researchers ID protein linked to heart recovery
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech researchers deploying AI tools for medical discovery demonstrates deep capability development in New River Valley outside traditional NoVA/Richmond hubs, with Carilion partnership signaling potential for distributed AI fluency through academic-clinical networks.
